enonce_intro_markdown:
**Section D : Essay**

Write an essay of between 250-300 words on **one** of the following topics:

questions.enonce_markdown: Modern technology has brought more harm than good to the society. Do you agree?
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
L'essai argumentatif de type "Do you agree?" exige une position claire annoncée dès l'introduction (accord, désaccord, ou position nuancée), défendue ensuite par des arguments illustrés d'exemples concrets dans le développement, avant une conclusion qui reprend cette position sans s'y contredire. Le respect du nombre de mots imposé (ici 250-300 mots) fait partie des critères de notation.

**Modèle de rédaction (environ 250 mots) :**

Modern technology has undeniably transformed the way people live, work and communicate, but I disagree that it has brought more harm than good to society.

First of all, technology has considerably improved communication and access to information. Thanks to mobile phones, computers and the internet, people can now reach relatives living abroad within seconds, and students can research any topic without having to travel to a library. This has broken down the barriers of distance that used to isolate communities.

Furthermore, technology has revolutionised healthcare. Modern equipment such as scanners, ventilators and computer-assisted surgery tools have saved countless lives that would have been lost a few decades ago. Vaccines developed with the help of advanced laboratory technology have also eradicated or controlled diseases that once killed millions.

It is true that technology has brought some problems, such as addiction to social media, cyberbullying and job losses caused by automation. However, these problems come from the misuse of technology, not from technology itself. A knife can be used to cook or to hurt someone; the tool is not to blame, the user is.

In conclusion, when we weigh the tremendous benefits technology has brought to education, health and communication against the problems caused mainly by its misuse, it becomes clear that modern technology has done far more good than harm to society. What is needed is not to reject technology, but to use it responsibly.

### Piège à éviter
Ne te contente pas d'une simple liste d'exemples ; chaque argument doit être développé et relié explicitement à la thèse annoncée en introduction, sinon le correcteur perçoit un manque de cohérence argumentative.

### Conseil
Compte approximativement tes mots pendant la rédaction (environ 5 lignes manuscrites = 50 mots) pour rester dans la fourchette imposée : un essai trop court ou trop long est pénalisé même s'il est bien écrit.

questions.enonce_markdown: The problems of youths and possible solutions.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Un essai "problèmes et solutions" doit énoncer clairement chaque problème avant de proposer, dans le même ordre, une solution qui lui correspond directement : le développement gagne à suivre une structure parallèle (problème 1 -> solution 1, problème 2 -> solution 2...) plutôt que de séparer tous les problèmes d'un côté et toutes les solutions de l'autre sans lien explicite.

**Modèle de rédaction (environ 250 mots) :**

Young people today face a number of serious problems that threaten their future and that of society as a whole.

The first major problem is unemployment. Many young graduates leave school with diplomas but cannot find jobs, which pushes some of them towards frustration, crime or even the search for greener pastures abroad through irregular migration. Secondly, drug and alcohol abuse have become common among youths, often as a way of escaping poverty, stress or peer pressure. Thirdly, many young people drop out of school early because their parents cannot afford school fees, or because they get involved in early pregnancy or delinquency.

These problems, however, are not without solutions. Governments should create more job opportunities by encouraging entrepreneurship and supporting small businesses run by young people, for instance through youth employment funds and vocational training centres. Schools and families should also organise sensitisation campaigns on the dangers of drug abuse, so that young people are well informed before falling into addiction. In addition, free or subsidised education should be extended to vulnerable children to reduce school dropout, and strict laws should be enforced against early marriage and child labour.

In conclusion, the problems of youths, though serious, can be solved if governments, schools, parents and the youths themselves work together. A country that invests in the well-being of its youths today is investing in its own future.

questions.enonce_markdown: You accompanied a hunter to a hunting expedition. Tell the story.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Un essai narratif se construit chronologiquement (début - milieu - fin), au passé, et se distingue de l'essai argumentatif par l'absence de thèse à défendre : l'objectif est de raconter une expérience vécue de façon vivante, avec des détails sensoriels (ce qu'on voit, entend, ressent) qui rendent le récit crédible.

**Modèle de rédaction (environ 250 mots) :**

Last dry season, my uncle, who is a well-known hunter in our village, invited me to accompany him on a hunting expedition into the forest. I was both excited and nervous, for it was going to be my very first time.

We set off very early in the morning, before the sun had risen, each of us carrying a bag with food, a torchlight and a machete. My uncle also carried his old hunting gun and called his two hunting dogs, Simba and Rex, to follow us. As we walked deeper into the forest, the tall trees blocked out most of the sunlight, and strange sounds of birds and insects filled the air.

After about two hours of walking, the dogs suddenly started barking furiously and ran towards a bush. My uncle signalled me to stay still and be quiet. Moments later, a wild antelope darted out of the bush, and before I could even blink, my uncle fired a single shot. The animal fell instantly. I was amazed at his skill and calmness under pressure.

We rested for a while, and my uncle taught me how to identify animal footprints and how to move silently in the forest. By early afternoon, we had also caught two bush rats in traps he had set the previous week.

Tired but thrilled, we finally returned home carrying our catch. That day taught me patience, courage and respect for nature, and I will never forget my first hunting expedition with my uncle.

### Conseil
Dans un récit, veille à garder le même temps du passé (past simple pour les actions principales, past continuous pour le décor ou une action en cours) du début à la fin : les changements de temps non justifiés sont l'erreur la plus fréquente et la plus pénalisée dans ce type d'essai.
